record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Topology of Manifolds
record.original_question: Complex conjugation on CP^2 has fixed set RP^2 and orbit space S^4, and the analogous involution on aCP^2 # bCP^2 gives a locally flat embedding of the connected sum of a+b copies of RP^2 in S^4. Is every locally flat topological embedding of a closed nonorientable surface in S^4 whose complement has fundamental group of order 2 homeomorphic to one of these embeddings?

evidence.quote: The involution on aCP2#bCP2 thus gives a locally flat embedding of #a+bRP2 in S4.
Conjecture. Any locally flat topological embedding of a closed nonorientable surface in S4 whose complement has order 2 fundamental group is homeomorphic to one of the above embeddings.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that complex conjugation on the complex projective plane $\mathbb{CP}^2$ is an orientation-preserving smooth involution whose fixed point set is $\mathbb{RP}^2$ and whose orbit space is homeomorphic to $S^4$; this exhibits a standard locally flat embedding of $\mathbb{RP}^2$ in $S^4$. More generally, for nonnegative integers $a,b$, the analogous involution on the connected sum $a\mathbb{CP}^2 \# b\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ has orbit space $S^4$ and fixed-point set the connected sum of $a+b$ copies of $\mathbb{RP}^2$, giving a locally flat topological embedding of the closed nonorientable surface $\#_{a+b}\mathbb{RP}^2$ into $S^4$. Call any embedding obtained in this way a standard embedding.

Prove or disprove: every locally flat topological embedding $F \hookrightarrow S^4$ of a closed nonorientable surface $F$ such that $\pi_1(S^4 \setminus F)$ has order $2$ is topologically equivalent (i.e., there is a self-homeomorphism of $S^4$ carrying one image onto the other) to a standard embedding as above.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Conway–Orson–Powell ("Unknotting nonorientable surfaces") establishes the conjecture for closed nonorientable surfaces in S^4 with knot group of order 2 whenever the normal Euler number is not extremal in Massey's range, and additionally for all normal Euler numbers when nonorientable genus h ≤ 3. Subsequent work extends the result to genera 4 and 5. The general case (all genera with extremal normal Euler number) appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Unknotting nonorientable surfaces (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: every such surface with knot group of order two is topologically unknotted, provided that the normal Euler number is not extremal in Massey's range; for h = 1, 2, or 3, the same holds even at extremal normal Euler number
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture proven in non-extremal Euler number cases and for low genus.

status_evidence.title: Unknotting nonorientable surfaces of genus 4 and 5
status_evidence.snippet: Closed, nonorientable, locally flatly embedded surfaces in S^4 with knot group of order 2 of nonorientable genus 4 and 5 are topologically unknotted.
status_evidence.claim: Extends the result to genera 4 and 5.
